A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICL Ciphers research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments across four datasets and six models, including cipher accuracy comparisons, sensitivity analyses, significance tests, and representation probing.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the accuracy tables and probing figures.

M1.justification: The bijective and non-bijective substitutions, Zipfian shuffling, priority sampling, and probing procedure remain unchanged. Noun-restricted shuffling in v2 Section 4.6 was already evaluated in v1 Appendix H.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SST-2, Amazon Reviews, HellaSwag, and WinoGrande with the same task coverage. The noun-only cipher scenario is retained from v1, not newly introduced.

E2.justification: The non-bijective control and comparator membership remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same pretrained model comparisons and the Llama 3.1 alignment and model-size comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported dataset splits, sample counts, accuracy metric, demonstration counts, shuffle rates, model configurations, and probing settings are unchanged. Moving the noun-only experiment into the main text introduces no new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The shuffle-rate, demonstration-count, alignment, model-size, sampling, and probing analyses are retained. V1 Appendix H and Table 10 become v2 Section 4.6 and Table 3, with the same noun-restriction experiment and measurements.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three runs and use McNemar's test with the same 0.05 significance threshold. Error-bar and significance-reporting practices are unchanged; the supplementary significance tables are renumbered.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, significance values, and plots are unchanged. For example, Llama 3.1 8B's 20-shot Amazon accuracies remain 64.7% and 72.3% for non-bijective and bijective ciphers. Noun-only HellaSwag accuracies remain 32.1% and 33.6% in v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 3.

T1.justification: The cipher definitions, reversibility reasoning, and rank-difference equation are retained. Writing g(x_i') instead of g in Section 2.3 clarifies notation without changing the mathematical argument. No proofs or formal results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and concluding paragraph retain the same central claims: a cipher-based framework for quantifying task learning, bijective advantages across four datasets and six models, and internal decoding evidence. The contribution's scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 2.5 and 6 newly explain that task success can rely on task-relevant token attributes without completely recovering the cipher. The noun-only experiment is reframed from investigating task complexity and mixed gap changes to grammatical roles and similar gaps, with a new assertion about preserving syntactic and semantic structure.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 drops the explicit instruction to randomly sample a demonstration for each selected token when m > n. This slightly reduces implementation detail without establishing a changed procedure. Dataset preparation, token filters, prompt templates, and the code repository link otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Section 5 adds explicit contamination concerns about Vacareanu et al. and Nafar et al., and stronger comparative claims about the framework's generality and reliability. Existing related-work material is also relocated into Appendix A.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized paragraph revisions, expands motivation and interpretation, promotes the noun-only analysis into the main text, consolidates related work in the supplement, and adds an appendix contents list. The overall narrative and most text remain intact.

P2.justification: The noun-only table moves from the appendix to the main text, other tables are renumbered, and supplementary figures and tables are regrouped near their discussions. Figure 1 is resized and Figure 4's caption expands. Existing graphical content and table designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a limited clarity and navigation improvement: Sections 2.5 and 6 explain partial, task-dependent deciphering, and the existing noun-only analysis and appendices are easier to locate. Empirical support is unchanged. These benefits are tempered by reduced sampling detail and stronger statements about semantic preservation and contamination that receive no additional validation.
